overall: The AG found the Sandwich Historic District Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law when it discussed an unlisted fence exemption, because the chair did not reasonably anticipate the topic 48 hours ahead; no abutter notice or public comment was required.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee discussed a Certificate of Exemption for a fence at its July 11 meeting, a topic not listed on the posted notice.
allegations.key_passage: As such, the chair did not reasonably anticipate that the Committee would discuss the Certificate of Exemption during the July 11 meeting, and therefore he was not required to list it in the meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee failed to give the complainant notice as an abutter before considering the fence application.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require public bodies to provide additional notice of meetings to specific individuals or groups of individuals for topics discussed during a meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee failed to provide an opportunity for public comment before considering the application.
allegations.key_passage: It is not a violation of the Open Meeting Law for a public body to vote on a topic without first taking comments from the public.
